proposal.hypothesis: A 16-byte SSE2 mask validator may reduce scalar control flow on the official mixed-width n=65536 input by classifying every byte lane, comparing continuation masks against shifted starter requirements with carry across blocks, and checking restricted second-byte ranges. A bounded scalar fallback from the last known code-point boundary handles the tail and any unfinished sequence. The SSE2 path is enabled only when the compiler target defines __SSE2__; otherwise the supplied scalar validator remains the control. This is a performance hypothesis, not a claimed speedup.

retained: Retained the supplied scalar validator as a control and fallback.
Added compile-time guarded 16-byte SSE2 lane classification for ASCII, continuation bytes, and legal two-, three-, and four-byte starters.
Compared shifted starter requirements with continuation masks while carrying cross-block continuation state.
Checked E0, ED, F0, and F4 second-byte bounds, including a pending bound at vector boundaries.
Used scalar validation from the last known code-point boundary for an incomplete vector tail; preserved the run ABI, output, and thread budget.

The experiment retains the exact exclusions for C0/C1 and F5-F7, as well as shifted continuation requirements, restricted second-byte checks, cross-block state, and scalar tail handling. Earlier evidence does not establish a speedup: the valid T1 ASCII-block variant measured 57.50 µs versus the 49.62 µs baseline, while a distinct valid T2 variant measured 39.98 µs. This classifier variant needs official evaluation.

Preserved shifted continuation checks, E0/ED/F0/F4 second-byte constraints, cross-block carry and pending state, safe scalar fallback boundaries, bounded tail handling, ABI, output, and thread budget.

proposal.hypothesis: The SSE2 path already classifies starters and continuation requirements across 16-byte blocks, but performs several SIMD comparisons to validate restricted second-byte ranges. Checking those ranges scalarly only for E0, ED, F0, or F4 starter lanes may reduce per-block SIMD work when those starters are infrequent. Lane-15 checks remain deferred across the block boundary, and the existing scalar validator remains the fallback/control. This is an unmeasured hybrid; the official mixed-width n=65536 timing will determine whether it helps.

retained: Retained the supplied scalar UTF-8 validator and the existing compile-time SSE2/scalar fallback.
Kept 16-byte SIMD starter classification, shifted continuation requirements, carry state, and bounded scalar tail handling.
Replaced vector-wide restricted second-byte range comparisons with conditional scalar checks only for E0, ED, F0, and F4 lanes.
Deferred restricted checks for lane 15 to the next vector while preserving exact second-byte restrictions and the existing ABI/output.
